issues.description: Command names disagree with feature-test names (underscore vs hyphen).
issues.detail: Commands are registered as quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload (qutebrowser auto-converts underscores to hyphens at the command line: quickmarks-reload). But quickmark_save above is singular. The new tests use :bookmarks-reload and :quickmarks-reload (plural), inconsistent with the existing singular pattern quickmark-add/quickmark-save. Pick one convention; the invariant 'command name matches sibling commands' is currently violated.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic: a parse failure leaves marks empty.
issues.detail: The invariant should be: after reload(), self.marks reflects either the new file or the previous state. Current code calls self.marks.clear() then re-parses; if _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises, marks is empty and changed has not been emitted with a coherent state. Build the new OrderedDict into a local, then swap on success.

issues.description: _init_lineparser is re-invoked on every reload, re-reading config and re-binding self._lineparser.
issues.detail: Calling _init_lineparser() from reload() recreates the LineParser each time rather than asking the existing parser to re-read from disk. This is asymptotically fine (O(n) in file size, as required) but conceptually muddled: construction-time setup is being reused as a refresh primitive. A dedicated reread method on the lineparser would be the literate choice.

issues.description: Missing loop invariant / docstring on reload().
issues.detail: The new reload() docstring is one line. For a method that mutates shared state and emits a signal, the reader deserves an explicit statement of the postcondition (marks equals the on-disk file's parsed contents; changed is emitted exactly once) and the failure mode. Literate-programming-grade comment is missing.

issues.description: Test does not assert that changed fires exactly once, nor cover the malformed-file path.
issues.detail: test_reload verifies the happy path and that changed fires at least once via wait_signal. It does not pin down 'exactly once' (relevant if reload were ever called mid-parse) and does not exercise a malformed reload, which is precisely where the atomicity concern above shows up. Proofs catch what tests miss; here a second test would catch what the proof misses.

issues.description: Two unnamed Scenario blocks added to the feature file.
issues.detail: The new BDD scenarios have empty titles ('Scenario:' with no name). Readability suffers when test reports list anonymous scenarios; a descriptive name ('Reloading bookmarks from disk') costs nothing and aids the reader, which is the Knuthian constraint.

review.summary: The change is small, well-scoped, and the refactor of __init__ to delegate to reload() is the right factoring. Two issues warrant attention before merge: command naming is inconsistent with sibling commands (quickmark-add vs the new quickmarks-reload, plural), and reload() is not atomic — a parse error mid-reload leaves marks empty rather than preserving the previous state. The remaining items are literate-programming nits: missing invariant in the docstring, anonymous BDD scenarios, and a test that doesn't exercise the failure path. UNDER-AUDITED on the atomicity invariant; NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on reload().
